verses.sanskrit: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् | देवीं सरस्वतीं चैव ततो जयमुदीरयेत् ||
verses.transliteration: nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam | devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva tato jayamudīrayet ||
verses.translation: Having bowed to Narayana, and to the supreme among men (Nara), and to the Goddess Sarasvati — then let one declare victory.
verses.hindi: नारायण को नमस्कार करके, नरोत्तम को और देवी सरस्वती को — तब जय बोलना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's mangalacharana (auspicious opening) invokes the Nara-Narayana pair alongside Sarasvati. Nara and Narayana are the twin seers of the Himalayas — the human and the divine aspects of a single reality, inseparable. Their invocation alongside Sarasvati (the goddess of speech, knowledge, and music) signals the Purana's central concerns: the relation between the human and divine, mediated through the sacred arts of language and music. Narada himself is the living embodiment of this conjunction: the divine sage who makes music his devotion.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वदा सर्वभावेन भजनीयो जनार्दनः | भक्त्या परमया चैव प्रेम्णा च परमेण च ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo janārdanaḥ | bhaktyā paramayā caiva premṇā ca parameṇa ca ||
verses.translation: Janardana (Vishnu) should be worshipped always, with all one's being — with supreme devotion and with the highest love.
verses.hindi: जनार्दन का सदा, सर्वभाव से, परम भक्ति से और परम प्रेम से भजन करना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: Three qualifiers pile upon one another: "sarvadā" (always — not just in puja or in difficulty), "sarvabhāvena" (with all one's being — not a compartmentalised religious activity but the whole person), "paramayā bhaktyā" (with supreme devotion) and "parameṇa premṇā" (with the highest love). The Narada Purana insists that bhakti is not a technique or a ritual but a total orientation of one's existence. Loving the divine "always and with all one's being" is not a demand — it is a description of what genuine bhakti is. When it is genuine, it is naturally total.

verses.sanskrit: सप्त स्वराः समुद्भूताः ब्रह्माण्डस्य नादतः | षड्जं च ऋषभं चैव गान्धारं मध्यमं तथा | पञ्चमं च धैवतं च निषादं सप्तमं विदुः ||
verses.transliteration: sapta svarāḥ samudbhūtāḥ brahmāṇḍasya nādataḥ | ṣaḍjaṃ ca ṛṣabhaṃ caiva gāndhāraṃ madhyamaṃ tathā | pañcamaṃ ca dhhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ saptamaṃ viduḥ ||
verses.translation: The seven notes arose from the sound of the cosmos — Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni — these seven are known.
verses.hindi: सात स्वर ब्रह्माण्ड के नाद से उत्पन्न हुए — षड्ज, ऋषभ, गान्धार, मध्यम, पञ्चम, धैवत, निषाद — ये सात जाने जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's cosmological account of the seven musical notes: they did not arise from human invention but from the primordial sound (nāda) of the cosmos itself — the vibration of the Brahmaanda (cosmic egg). Each note is thus not an acoustic convention but a frequency of existence. Sa (Shadja — born from six) is the tonic, the ground; each subsequent note is a specific relationship to that ground. The entire raga system is a map of how consciousness moves away from and returns to its own source. Narada's teaching: when you sing in tune, you are resonating with the structure of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवपूजनम् | वैश्वदेवं तथातिथ्यं नित्यकर्मेति कीर्तितम् ||
verses.transliteration: snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devapūjanam | vaiśvadevaṃ tathātithyaṃ nityakarmeti kīrtitam ||
verses.translation: Bathing, giving, japa, fire-offering, self-study, worship of the deity, the Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings), and hospitality — these are declared the daily duties (nitya-karma).
verses.hindi: स्नान, दान, जप, होम, स्वाध्याय, देवपूजन, वैश्वदेव और अतिथि-सेवा — ये नित्यकर्म कहे गये हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's eight-fold daily practice — nitya-karma — is a complete architecture of a life oriented toward the divine. Snana (purification of body), dana (purification through giving), japa (purification of speech/mind through repetition), homa (fire-offering — the discipline of sacrifice), svadhyaya (self-study — reading and contemplating the sacred), deva-pujana (formal worship), Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings — the recognition of the divine in all forms of life), and atithya (hospitality — honouring the divine in the stranger). Together these eight cover the full range of human activity: body, resources, mind, speech, knowledge, ritual, ecology, and social relationship.

verses.sanskrit: नामैकं यस्य वाचि स्मरणपथगतं श्रोत्रमूलं गतं वा | शुद्धं वाशुद्धवर्णं विगतमतिभयं तारयत्येव सिन्धुम् ||
verses.transliteration: nāmaikaṃ yasya vāci smaraṇapathagatāṃ śrotramūlaṃ gataṃ vā | śuddhaṃ vāśuddhavarṇaṃ vigatamātibhayaṃ tārayatyeva sindhum ||
verses.translation: The one name — whether spoken by the voice, whether reached by memory, whether it has entered the root of the ear — pure or impure in pronunciation — crossing all fear, it carries one across the ocean.
verses.hindi: वह एक नाम — चाहे वाणी से बोला जाये, चाहे स्मरण-पथ से प्राप्त हो, चाहे कान की जड़ तक पहुँचे — शुद्ध हो या अशुद्ध उच्चारण — सभी भय को पार करके, वह सागर को पार कराता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana makes the most inclusive possible claim for nama-japa: it works whether spoken, silently remembered, or even merely heard. And — crucially — whether the pronunciation is "pure" (śuddhaṃ) or "impure" (aśuddhavarṇaṃ). This directly addresses the anxiety that non-Sanskritists or those uncertain of correct pronunciation feel about mantra practice. The divine name is not a code that only works when decoded correctly; it is a living reality that responds to the love behind the utterance, not the linguistic precision of it.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He who worships Vishnu with devotion attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। जो विष्णु को भक्ति से भजता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. "Divyadūta" — divine messenger. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana's core teaching: Narada is not merely a sage but the divine messenger who initiates the bhakti path, and devotion to Vishnu is the means of liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. verses.sanskrit: संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम संकीर्तनं नाम तथा | संकीर्तनं नाम स्मरणं संकीर्तनं नाम भक्तिः ||
verses.transliteration: saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma tathā | saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma smaraṇaṃ saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma bhaktiḥ ||
verses.translation: Sankirtana of Vishnu's name, sankirtana of the name, sankirtana of remembrance, sankirtana of devotion — all are sankirtana.
verses.hindi: विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन, नाम का संकीर्तन, स्मरण का संकीर्तन, भक्ति का संकीर्तन — सब संकीर्तन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. The Narada Purana places sankirtana at the center of the bhakti path.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. verses.sanskrit: गायति वादति नृत्यति पूजयति शृणोति च | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: gāyati vādati nṛtyati pūjayati śṛṇoti ca | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, listening — he who worships Vishnu with devotion through these attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: गाते, बोलते, नृत्य करते, पूजा करते, सुनते — जो इन सब से भक्ति से विष्णु का भजन करता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. The verse states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion through these five forms attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana teaching that bhakti can be expressed through multiple modalities. All are valid paths to liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः | ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ||
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ | tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram ||
verses.translation: Through bhakti one truly knows Me — what I am and how great I am. Having thus truly known Me, one enters into Me immediately after.
verses.hindi: भक्ति से मुझे यथार्थ जाना जाता है — जितना मैं हूँ और जैसा मैं हूँ। इस प्रकार मुझे तत्त्वतः जानकर, वह तत्पश्चात् मुझमें प्रवेश करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana quotes the Bhagavad Gita (18.55) as its ultimate authority — Vishnu's own declaration that bhakti is the means of truly knowing the divine, and that this knowledge leads directly to entry (viśate) into the divine. "Tattvataḥ" — truly, in reality, as it actually is — distinguishes this knowing from intellectual knowledge about the divine. Intellectual knowledge describes; bhakti-jnana reveals. The sequence is precise: bhakti → tattvataḥ-jnanam → entry into the divine. The Narada Purana places this Gita verse at the culmination of its Uttara Khanda to complete the arc: from the nine forms of bhakti, through sankirtana, through music, through the five forms of the divine, through daily practice — everything converges on this single verse.

verses.sanskrit: श्रवणं कीर्तनं विष्णोः स्मरणं पादसेवनम् | अर्चनं वन्दनं दास्यं सख्यमात्मनिवेदनम् ||
verses.transliteration: śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṃ pādasavanam | arcanaṃ vandanaṃ dāsyaṃ sakhyamātmanivedanam ||
verses.translation: Hearing, chanting, remembering Vishnu, serving his feet, worship, obeisance, servitude, friendship, and complete self-surrender — these nine are the forms of devotion.
verses.hindi: श्रवण, कीर्तन, विष्णु का स्मरण, पादसेवन, अर्चन, वन्दन, दास्य, सख्य और आत्मनिवेदन — ये नव प्रकार की भक्ति हैं।
verses.commentary: The most famous verse of the entire bhakti tradition — cited in the Bhagavata Purana (7.5.23-24) and originating in the Narada Purana. The nine forms cover the complete spectrum of human relational modes: intellectual (shravanam — hearing, taking in), vocal/communal (kirtanam — singing together), contemplative (smaranam — holding in mind), physical service (padasavanam), ritual (archanam), reverential (vandanam), relational as servant (dasyam), relational as friend (sakhyam), and the complete dissolution of separate selfhood (atma-nivedanam). Every human being has access to at least one of these nine natural entry points.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र मनो याति तत्र तत्र समाहितम् | तत्र तत्र परं ब्रह्म तत्र तत्र जनार्दनः ||
verses.transliteration: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatra samāhitam | tatra tatra paraṃ brahma tatra tatra janārdanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Wherever the mind goes — there is the collected (concentrated one). There is supreme Brahman there. There is Janardana (Vishnu) there.
verses.hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ मन जाता है — वहाँ-वहाँ वह समाहित (एकाग्र) है। वहाँ-वहाँ परम ब्रह्म है। वहाँ-वहाँ जनार्दन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's radical teaching on the ubiquity of the divine: wherever the mind moves, Brahman is already there. This is not a consolation but a metaphysical assertion. If Brahman is truly all-pervading (vibhu, sarvavyapin), then there is no location — mental or physical — where Brahman is absent. The implication for bhakti is transformative: you cannot leave the divine. You can only fail to notice it. The practice of smaranam (remembrance) is thus not about bringing the divine into consciousness but about recognising what is already and always present there.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम गायति वादति नृत्यति ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma gāyati vādati nṛtyati ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He sings, speaks, and dances the sankirtana of Vishnu's name.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। वे विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन गाते, बोलते और नृत्य करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. Bhakti is not merely private devotion but public celebration — singing, speaking, dancing. Narada represents the archetype of the divine communicator who spreads the name of Vishnu everywhere. The Narada Purana places sankirtana (chanting) at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वदा सर्वभावेन भजनीयो जनार्दनः | भक्त्या परमया चैव प्रेम्णा च परमेण च ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo janārdanaḥ | bhaktyā paramayā caiva premṇā ca parameṇa ca ||
verses.translation: Janardana (Vishnu) should be worshipped always, with all one's being — with supreme devotion and with the highest love.
verses.hindi: जनार्दन का सदा, सर्वभाव से, परम भक्ति से और परम प्रेम से भजन करना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: Three qualifiers pile upon one another: "sarvadā" (always — not just in puja or in difficulty), "sarvabhāvena" (with all one's being — not a compartmentalised religious activity but the whole person), "paramayā bhaktyā" (with supreme devotion) and "parameṇa premṇā" (with the highest love). The Narada Purana insists that bhakti is not a technique or a ritual but a total orientation of one's existence. Loving the divine "always and with all one's being" is not a demand — it is a description of what genuine bhakti is. When it is genuine, it is naturally total.

verses.sanskrit: स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवपूजनम् | वैश्वदेवं तथातिथ्यं नित्यकर्मेति कीर्तितम् ||
verses.transliteration: snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devapūjanam | vaiśvadevaṃ tathātithyaṃ nityakarmeti kīrtitam ||
verses.translation: Bathing, giving, japa, fire-offering, self-study, worship of the deity, the Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings), and hospitality — these are declared the daily duties (nitya-karma).
verses.hindi: स्नान, दान, जप, होम, स्वाध्याय, देवपूजन, वैश्वदेव और अतिथि-सेवा — ये नित्यकर्म कहे गये हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's eight-fold daily practice — nitya-karma — is a complete architecture of a life oriented toward the divine. Snana (purification of body), dana (purification through giving), japa (purification of speech/mind through repetition), homa (fire-offering — the discipline of sacrifice), svadhyaya (self-study — reading and contemplating the sacred), deva-pujana (formal worship), Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings — the recognition of the divine in all forms of life), and atithya (hospitality — honouring the divine in the stranger). Together these eight cover the full range of human activity: body, resources, mind, speech, knowledge, ritual, ecology, and social relationship.

verses.sanskrit: नामैकं यस्य वाचि स्मरणपथगतं श्रोत्रमूलं गतं वा | शुद्धं वाशुद्धवर्णं विगतमतिभयं तारयत्येव सिन्धुम् ||
verses.transliteration: nāmaikaṃ yasya vāci smaraṇapathagatāṃ śrotramūlaṃ gataṃ vā | śuddhaṃ vāśuddhavarṇaṃ vigatamātibhayaṃ tārayatyeva sindhum ||
verses.translation: The one name — whether spoken by the voice, whether reached by memory, whether it has entered the root of the ear — pure or impure in pronunciation — crossing all fear, it carries one across the ocean.
verses.hindi: वह एक नाम — चाहे वाणी से बोला जाये, चाहे स्मरण-पथ से प्राप्त हो, चाहे कान की जड़ तक पहुँचे — शुद्ध हो या अशुद्ध उच्चारण — सभी भय को पार करके, वह सागर को पार कराता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana makes the most inclusive possible claim for nama-japa: it works whether spoken, silently remembered, or even merely heard. And — crucially — whether the pronunciation is "pure" (śuddhaṃ) or "impure" (aśuddhavarṇaṃ). This directly addresses the anxiety that non-Sanskritists or those uncertain of correct pronunciation feel about mantra practice. The divine name is not a code that only works when decoded correctly; it is a living reality that responds to the love behind the utterance, not the linguistic precision of it.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He who worships Vishnu with devotion attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। जो विष्णु को भक्ति से भजता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. "Divyadūta" — divine messenger. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana's core teaching: Narada is not merely a sage but the divine messenger who initiates the bhakti path, and devotion to Vishnu is the means of liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. "Divyadūta" — divine messenger. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state. verses.sanskrit: संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम संकीर्तनं नाम तथा | संकीर्तनं नाम स्मरणं संकीर्तनं नाम भक्तिः ||
verses.transliteration: saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma tathā | saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma smaraṇaṃ saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma bhaktiḥ ||
verses.translation: Sankirtana of Vishnu's name, sankirtana of the name, sankirtana of remembrance, sankirtana of devotion — all are sankirtana.
verses.hindi: विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन, नाम का संकीर्तन, स्मरण का संकीर्तन, भक्ति का संकीर्तन — सब संकीर्तन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. The Narada Purana places sankirtana at the center of the bhakti path.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. verses.sanskrit: गायति वादति नृत्यति पूजयति शृणोति च | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: gāyati vādati nṛtyati pūjayati śṛṇoti ca | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, listening — he who worships Vishnu with devotion through these attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: गाते, बोलते, नृत्य करते, पूजा करते, सुनते — जो इन सब से भक्ति से विष्णु का भजन करता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. The verse states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion through these five forms attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana teaching that bhakti can be expressed through multiple modalities. All are valid paths to liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः | ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ||
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ | tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram ||
verses.translation: Through bhakti one truly knows Me — what I am and how great I am. Having thus truly known Me, one enters into Me immediately after.
verses.hindi: भक्ति से मुझे यथार्थ जाना जाता है — जितना मैं हूँ और जैसा मैं हूँ। इस प्रकार मुझे तत्त्वतः जानकर, वह तत्पश्चात् मुझमें प्रवेश करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana quotes the Bhagavad Gita (18.55) as its ultimate authority — Vishnu's own declaration that bhakti is the means of truly knowing the divine, and that this knowledge leads directly to entry (viśate) into the divine. "Tattvataḥ" — truly, in reality, as it actually is — distinguishes this knowing from intellectual knowledge about the divine. Intellectual knowledge describes; bhakti-jnana reveals. The sequence is precise: bhakti → tattvataḥ-jnanam → entry into the divine. The Narada Purana places this Gita verse at the culmination of its Uttara Khanda to complete the arc: from the nine forms of bhakti, through sankirtana, through music, through the five forms of the divine, through daily practice — everything converges on this single verse.

verses.sanskrit: हरेर्नाम हरेर्नाम हरेर्नामैव केवलम् | कलौ नास्त्येव नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरन्यथा ||
verses.transliteration: harernāma harernāma harernāmaiva kevalam | kalau nāstyeva nāstyeva nāstyeva gatiranyathā ||
verses.translation: The name of Hari, the name of Hari, the name of Hari alone — in Kali Yuga there is no other way, no other way, no other way.
verses.hindi: हरि का नाम, हरि का नाम, हरि का नाम ही केवल — कलियुग में कोई अन्य मार्ग नहीं है, नहीं है, नहीं है।
verses.commentary: The most famous verse of the Narada Purana — and one of the most recognisable in all of devotional Hinduism. Three repetitions of the name, three repetitions of the negation: the rhetorical structure enacts the teaching. The name itself is repeated three times before the instruction, as if to demonstrate rather than merely describe. "Kevalam" — alone, only, purely — leaves no room for hedging. This is not the Narada Purana claiming other paths are wrong; it is claiming that for the specific conditions of Kali Yuga (fragmented attention, shortened lifespans, weakened tapas-capacity), the nama alone is the universally accessible and universally sufficient path.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम गायति वादति नृत्यति ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma gāyati vādati nṛtyati ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He sings, speaks, and dances the sankirtana of Vishnu's name.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। वे विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन गाते, बोलते और नृत्य करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. Bhakti is not merely private devotion but public celebration — singing, speaking, dancing. Narada represents the archetype of the divine communicator who spreads the name of Vishnu everywhere. The Narada Purana places sankirtana (chanting) at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: सप्त स्वराः समुद्भूताः ब्रह्माण्डस्य नादतः | षड्जं च ऋषभं चैव गान्धारं मध्यमं तथा | पञ्चमं च धैवतं च निषादं सप्तमं विदुः ||
verses.transliteration: sapta svarāḥ samudbhūtāḥ brahmāṇḍasya nādataḥ | ṣaḍjaṃ ca ṛṣabhaṃ caiva gāndhāraṃ madhyamaṃ tathā | pañcamaṃ ca dhhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ saptamaṃ viduḥ ||
verses.translation: The seven notes arose from the sound of the cosmos — Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni — these seven are known.
verses.hindi: सात स्वर ब्रह्माण्ड के नाद से उत्पन्न हुए — षड्ज, ऋषभ, गान्धार, मध्यम, पञ्चम, धैवत, निषाद — ये सात जाने जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's cosmological account of the seven musical notes: they did not arise from human invention but from the primordial sound (nāda) of the cosmos itself — the vibration of the Brahmaanda (cosmic egg). Each note is thus not an acoustic convention but a frequency of existence. Sa (Shadja — born from six) is the tonic, the ground; each subsequent note is a specific relationship to that ground. The entire raga system is a map of how consciousness moves away from and returns to its own source. Narada's teaching: when you sing in tune, you are resonating with the structure of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र मनो याति तत्र तत्र समाहितम् | तत्र तत्र परं ब्रह्म तत्र तत्र जनार्दनः ||
verses.transliteration: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatra samāhitam | tatra tatra paraṃ brahma tatra tatra janārdanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Wherever the mind goes — there is the collected (concentrated one). There is supreme Brahman there. There is Janardana (Vishnu) there.
verses.hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ मन जाता है — वहाँ-वहाँ वह समाहित (एकाग्र) है। वहाँ-वहाँ परम ब्रह्म है। वहाँ-वहाँ जनार्दन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's radical teaching on the ubiquity of the divine: wherever the mind moves, Brahman is already there. This is not a consolation but a metaphysical assertion. If Brahman is truly all-pervading (vibhu, sarvavyapin), then there is no location — mental or physical — where Brahman is absent. The implication for bhakti is transformative: you cannot leave the divine. You can only fail to notice it. The practice of smaranam (remembrance) is thus not about bringing the divine into consciousness but about recognising what is already and always present there.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वदा सर्वभावेन भजनीयो जनार्दनः | भक्त्या परमया चैव प्रेम्णा च परमेण च ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo janārdanaḥ | bhaktyā paramayā caiva premṇā ca parameṇa ca ||
verses.translation: Janardana (Vishnu) should be worshipped always, with all one's being — with supreme devotion and with the highest love.
verses.hindi: जनार्दन का सदा, सर्वभाव से, परम भक्ति से और परम प्रेम से भजन करना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: Three qualifiers pile upon one another: "sarvadā" (always — not just in puja or in difficulty), "sarvabhāvena" (with all one's being — not a compartmentalised religious activity but the whole person), "paramayā bhaktyā" (with supreme devotion) and "parameṇa premṇā" (with the highest love). The Narada Purana insists that bhakti is not a technique or a ritual but a total orientation of one's existence. Loving the divine "always and with all one's being" is not a demand — it is a description of what genuine bhakti is. When it is genuine, it is naturally total.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He who worships Vishnu with devotion attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। जो विष्णु को भक्ति से भजता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. "Divyadūta" — divine messenger. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana's core teaching: Narada is not merely a sage but the divine messenger who initiates the bhakti path, and devotion to Vishnu is the means of liberation.

verses.sanskrit: संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम संकीर्तनं नाम तथा | संकीर्तनं नाम स्मरणं संकीर्तनं नाम भक्तिः ||
verses.transliteration: saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma tathā | saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma smaraṇaṃ saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma bhaktiḥ ||
verses.translation: Sankirtana of Vishnu's name, sankirtana of the name, sankirtana of remembrance, sankirtana of devotion — all are sankirtana.
verses.hindi: विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन, नाम का संकीर्तन, स्मरण का संकीर्तन, भक्ति का संकीर्तन — सब संकीर्तन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. The Narada Purana places sankirtana at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: गायति वादति नृत्यति पूजयति शृणोति च | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: gāyati vādati nṛtyati pūjayati śṛṇoti ca | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, listening — he who worships Vishnu with devotion through these attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: गाते, बोलते, नृत्य करते, पूजा करते, सुनते — जो इन सब से भक्ति से विष्णु का भजन करता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. The verse states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion through these five forms attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana teaching that bhakti can be expressed through multiple modalities. All are valid paths to liberation.

verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः | ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ||
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ | tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram ||
verses.translation: Through bhakti one truly knows Me — what I am and how great I am. Having thus truly known Me, one enters into Me immediately after.
verses.hindi: भक्ति से मुझे यथार्थ जाना जाता है — जितना मैं हूँ और जैसा मैं हूँ। इस प्रकार मुझे तत्त्वतः जानकर, वह तत्पश्चात् मुझमें प्रवेश करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana quotes the Bhagavad Gita (18.55) as its ultimate authority — Vishnu's own declaration that bhakti is the means of truly knowing the divine, and that this knowledge leads directly to entry (viśate) into the divine. "Tattvataḥ" — truly, in reality, as it actually is — distinguishes this knowing from intellectual knowledge about the divine. Intellectual knowledge describes; bhakti-jnana reveals. The sequence is precise: bhakti → tattvataḥ-jnanam → entry into the divine. The Narada Purana places this Gita verse at the culmination of its Uttara Khanda to complete the arc: from the nine forms of bhakti, through sankirtana, through music, through the five forms of the divine, through daily practice — everything converges on this single verse.

verses.sanskrit: संगीतज्ञानमादाय पठित्वा सर्वशास्त्रतः | ब्रह्मज्ञानं समाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ||
verses.transliteration: saṃgītajñānamādāya paṭhitvā sarvaśāstrata | brahmajñānaṃ samāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
verses.translation: Having obtained the knowledge of music, having studied all the shastras — one attains the knowledge of Brahman. No deliberation need be made about this.
verses.hindi: संगीत का ज्ञान प्राप्त करके, सभी शास्त्रों का अध्ययन करके — ब्रह्मज्ञान की प्राप्ति होती है। इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's most audacious claim: sangita-jnana leads to Brahma-jnana. Music-knowledge leads to the knowledge of Brahman. This is not metaphor. Narada's teaching is that the practitioner of deep musical attainment — who has mastered not just the technical but the experiential dimension of music — arrives at the same recognition that the Vedanta philosopher arrives at through analysis. The raga is a map of consciousness; the performance is a meditation; the dissolution of the musician into the music is the dissolution of ego into Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: सप्त स्वराः समुद्भूताः ब्रह्माण्डस्य नादतः | षड्जं च ऋषभं चैव गान्धारं मध्यमं तथा | पञ्चमं च धैवतं च निषादं सप्तमं विदुः ||
verses.transliteration: sapta svarāḥ samudbhūtāḥ brahmāṇḍasya nādataḥ | ṣaḍjaṃ ca ṛṣabhaṃ caiva gāndhāraṃ madhyamaṃ tathā | pañcamaṃ ca dhhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ saptamaṃ viduḥ ||
verses.translation: The seven notes arose from the sound of the cosmos — Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni — these seven are known.
verses.hindi: सात स्वर ब्रह्माण्ड के नाद से उत्पन्न हुए — षड्ज, ऋषभ, गान्धार, मध्यम, पञ्चम, धैवत, निषाद — ये सात जाने जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's cosmological account of the seven musical notes: they did not arise from human invention but from the primordial sound (nāda) of the cosmos itself — the vibration of the Brahmaanda (cosmic egg). Each note is thus not an acoustic convention but a frequency of existence. Sa (Shadja — born from six) is the tonic, the ground; each subsequent note is a specific relationship to that ground. The entire raga system is a map of how consciousness moves away from and returns to its own source. Narada's teaching: when you sing in tune, you are resonating with the structure of the universe.

verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma gāyati vādati nṛtyati ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He sings, speaks, and dances the sankirtana of Vishnu's name.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। वे विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन गाते, बोलते और नृत्य करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. Bhakti is not merely private devotion but public celebration — singing, speaking, dancing. Narada represents the archetype of the divine communicator who spreads the name of Vishnu everywhere. The Narada Purana places sankirtana (chanting) at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र मनो याति तत्र तत्र समाहितम् | तत्र तत्र परं ब्रह्म तत्र तत्र जनार्दनः ||
verses.transliteration: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatra samāhitam | tatra tatra paraṃ brahma tatra tatra janārdanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Wherever the mind goes — there is the collected (concentrated one). There is supreme Brahman there. There is Janardana (Vishnu) there.
verses.hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ मन जाता है — वहाँ-वहाँ वह समाहित (एकाग्र) है। वहाँ-वहाँ परम ब्रह्म है। वहाँ-वहाँ जनार्दन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's radical teaching on the ubiquity of the divine: wherever the mind moves, Brahman is already there. This is not a consolation but a metaphysical assertion. If Brahman is truly all-pervading (vibhu, sarvavyapin), then there is no location — mental or physical — where Brahman is absent. The implication for bhakti is transformative: you cannot leave the divine. You can only fail to notice it. The practice of smaranam (remembrance) is thus not about bringing the divine into consciousness but about recognising what is already and always present there.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वदा सर्वभावेन भजनीयो जनार्दनः | भक्त्या परमया चैव प्रेम्णा च परमेण च ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo janārdanaḥ | bhaktyā paramayā caiva premṇā ca parameṇa ca ||
verses.translation: Janardana (Vishnu) should be worshipped always, with all one's being — with supreme devotion and with the highest love.
verses.hindi: जनार्दन का सदा, सर्वभाव से, परम भक्ति से और परम प्रेम से भजन करना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: Three qualifiers pile upon one another: "sarvadā" (always — not just in puja or in difficulty), "sarvabhāvena" (with all one's being — not a compartmentalised religious activity but the whole person), "paramayā bhaktyā" (with supreme devotion) and "parameṇa premṇā" (with the highest love). The Narada Purana insists that bhakti is not a technique or a ritual but a total orientation of one's existence. Loving the divine "always and with all one's being" is not a demand — it is a description of what genuine bhakti is. When it is genuine, it is naturally total.

verses.sanskrit: नामैकं यस्य वाचि स्मरणपथगतं श्रोत्रमूलं गतं वा | शुद्धं वाशुद्धवर्णं विगतमतिभयं तारयत्येव सिन्धुम् ||
verses.transliteration: nāmaikaṃ yasya vāci smaraṇapathagatāṃ śrotramūlaṃ gataṃ vā | śuddhaṃ vāśuddhavarṇaṃ vigatamātibhayaṃ tārayatyeva sindhum ||
verses.translation: The one name — whether spoken by the voice, whether reached by memory, whether it has entered the root of the ear — pure or impure in pronunciation — crossing all fear, it carries one across the ocean.
verses.hindi: वह एक नाम — चाहे वाणी से बोला जाये, चाहे स्मरण-पथ से प्राप्त हो, चाहे कान की जड़ तक पहुँचे — शुद्ध हो या अशुद्ध उच्चारण — सभी भय को पार करके, वह सागर को पार कराता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana makes the most inclusive possible claim for nama-japa: it works whether spoken, silently remembered, or even merely heard. And — crucially — whether the pronunciation is "pure" (śuddhaṃ) or "impure" (aśuddhavarṇaṃ). This directly addresses the anxiety that non-Sanskritists or those uncertain of correct pronunciation feel about mantra practice. The divine name is not a code that only works when decoded correctly; it is a living reality that responds to the love behind the utterance, not the linguistic precision of it.

verses.transliteration: saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma tathā | saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma smaraṇaṃ saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma bhaktiḥ ||
verses.translation: Sankirtana of Vishnu's name, sankirtana of the name, sankirtana of remembrance, sankirtana of devotion — all are sankirtana.
verses.hindi: विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन, नाम का संकीर्तन, स्मरण का संकीर्तन, भक्ति का संकीर्तन — सब संकीर्तन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. The Narada Purana places sankirtana at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: गायति वादति नृत्यति पूजयति शृणोति च | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: gāyati vādati nṛtyati pūjayati śṛṇoti ca | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, listening — he who worships Vishnu with devotion through these attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: गाते, बोलते, नृत्य करते, पूजा करते, सुनते — जो इन सब से भक्ति से विष्णु का भजन करता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. The verse states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion through these five forms attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana teaching that bhakti can be expressed through multiple modalities. All are valid paths to liberation.

verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः | ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ||
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ | tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram ||
verses.translation: Through bhakti one truly knows Me — what I am and how great I am. Having thus truly known Me, one enters into Me immediately after.
verses.hindi: भक्ति से मुझे यथार्थ जाना जाता है — जितना मैं हूँ और जैसा मैं हूँ। इस प्रकार मुझे तत्त्वतः जानकर, वह तत्पश्चात् मुझमें प्रवेश करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana quotes the Bhagavad Gita (18.55) as its ultimate authority — Vishnu's own declaration that bhakti is the means of truly knowing the divine, and that this knowledge leads directly to entry (viśate) into the divine. "Tattvataḥ" — truly, in reality, as it actually is — distinguishes this knowing from intellectual knowledge about the divine. Intellectual knowledge describes; bhakti-jnana reveals. The sequence is precise: bhakti → tattvataḥ-jnanam → entry into the divine. The Narada Purana places this Gita verse at the culmination of its Uttara Khanda to complete the arc: from the nine forms of bhakti, through sankirtana, through music, through the five forms of the divine, through daily practice — everything converges on this single verse.

verses.sanskrit: परो व्यूहश्च विभवो ह्यन्तर्यामी तथार्चनम् | पञ्चधा वर्तते विष्णुः भक्तानुग्रहकारणात् ||
verses.transliteration: paro vyūhaśca vibhavo hyantaryāmī tathārchanam | pañcadhā vartate viṣṇuḥ bhaktānugrahakāraṇāt ||
verses.translation: Para, Vyuha, Vibhava, Antaryamin, and Archa — Vishnu exists in five forms, for the purpose of granting grace to the devotees.
verses.hindi: पर, व्यूह, विभव, अन्तर्यामी और अर्च — विष्णु पाँच रूपों में स्थित हैं, भक्तों पर अनुग्रह करने के लिए।
verses.commentary: The Pancharatra's five-fold structure of divine self-manifestation is among the most sophisticated theological frameworks in the Hindu tradition. Para — the transcendent, beyond all form, unknowable by the mind. Vyuha — the cosmic quartet of Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha, governing creation, preservation, and dissolution. Vibhava — the avatars, specific descents into historical time. Antaryamin — the indwelling presence in all beings. Archa — the consecrated image in the temple. The crucial point: each form is not less real than the previous — they are the same reality at different levels of accessibility. The Archa is not a "lower" form of the Para; it is the Para made available at the human level.

verses.sanskrit: स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवपूजनम् | वैश्वदेवं तथातिथ्यं नित्यकर्मेति कीर्तितम् ||
verses.transliteration: snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devapūjanam | vaiśvadevaṃ tathātithyaṃ nityakarmeti kīrtitam ||
verses.translation: Bathing, giving, japa, fire-offering, self-study, worship of the deity, the Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings), and hospitality — these are declared the daily duties (nitya-karma).
verses.hindi: स्नान, दान, जप, होम, स्वाध्याय, देवपूजन, वैश्वदेव और अतिथि-सेवा — ये नित्यकर्म कहे गये हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's eight-fold daily practice — nitya-karma — is a complete architecture of a life oriented toward the divine. Snana (purification of body), dana (purification through giving), japa (purification of speech/mind through repetition), homa (fire-offering — the discipline of sacrifice), svadhyaya (self-study — reading and contemplating the sacred), deva-pujana (formal worship), Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings — the recognition of the divine in all forms of life), and atithya (hospitality — honouring the divine in the stranger). Together these eight cover the full range of human activity: body, resources, mind, speech, knowledge, ritual, ecology, and social relationship.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम गायति वादति नृत्यति ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma gāyati vādati nṛtyati ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He sings, speaks, and dances the sankirtana of Vishnu's name.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। वे विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन गाते, बोलते और नृत्य करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. Bhakti is not merely private devotion but public celebration — singing, speaking, dancing. Narada represents the archetype of the divine communicator who spreads the name of Vishnu everywhere. The Narada Purana places sankirtana (chanting) at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: सप्त स्वराः समुद्भूताः ब्रह्माण्डस्य नादतः | षड्जं च ऋषभं चैव गान्धारं मध्यमं तथा | पञ्चमं च धैवतं च निषादं सप्तमं विदुः ||
verses.transliteration: sapta svarāḥ samudbhūtāḥ brahmāṇḍasya nādataḥ | ṣaḍjaṃ ca ṛṣabhaṃ caiva gāndhāraṃ madhyamaṃ tathā | pañcamaṃ ca dhhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ saptamaṃ viduḥ ||
verses.translation: The seven notes arose from the sound of the cosmos — Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni — these seven are known.
verses.hindi: सात स्वर ब्रह्माण्ड के नाद से उत्पन्न हुए — षड्ज, ऋषभ, गान्धार, मध्यम, पञ्चम, धैवत, निषाद — ये सात जाने जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's cosmological account of the seven musical notes: they did not arise from human invention but from the primordial sound (nāda) of the cosmos itself — the vibration of the Brahmaanda (cosmic egg). Each note is thus not an acoustic convention but a frequency of existence. Sa (Shadja — born from six) is the tonic, the ground; each subsequent note is a specific relationship to that ground. The entire raga system is a map of how consciousness moves away from and returns to its own source. Narada's teaching: when you sing in tune, you are resonating with the structure of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र मनो याति तत्र तत्र समाहितम् | तत्र तत्र परं ब्रह्म तत्र तत्र जनार्दनः ||
verses.transliteration: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatra samāhitam | tatra tatra paraṃ brahma tatra tatra janārdanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Wherever the mind goes — there is the collected (concentrated one). There is supreme Brahman there. There is Janardana (Vishnu) there.
verses.hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ मन जाता है — वहाँ-वहाँ वह समाहित (एकाग्र) है। वहाँ-वहाँ परम ब्रह्म है। वहाँ-वहाँ जनार्दन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's radical teaching on the ubiquity of the divine: wherever the mind moves, Brahman is already there. This is not a consolation but a metaphysical assertion. If Brahman is truly all-pervading (vibhu, sarvavyapin), then there is no location — mental or physical — where Brahman is absent. The implication for bhakti is transformative: you cannot leave the divine. You can only fail to notice it. The practice of smaranam (remembrance) is thus not about bringing the divine into consciousness but about recognising what is already and always present there.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वदा सर्वभावेन भजनीयो जनार्दनः | भक्त्या परमया चैव प्रेम्णा च परमेण च ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo janārdanaḥ | bhaktyā paramayā caiva premṇā ca parameṇa ca ||
verses.translation: Janardana (Vishnu) should be worshipped always, with all one's being — with supreme devotion and with the highest love.
verses.hindi: जनार्दन का सदा, सर्वभाव से, परम भक्ति से और परम प्रेम से भजन करना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: Three qualifiers pile upon one another: "sarvadā" (always — not just in puja or in difficulty), "sarvabhāvena" (with all one's being — not a compartmentalised religious activity but the whole person), "paramayā bhaktyā" (with supreme devotion) and "parameṇa premṇā" (with the highest love). The Narada Purana insists that bhakti is not a technique or a ritual but a total orientation of one's existence. Loving the divine "always and with all one's being" is not a demand — it is a description of what genuine bhakti is. When it is genuine, it is naturally total.

verses.sanskrit: नामैकं यस्य वाचि स्मरणपथगतं श्रोत्रमूलं गतं वा | शुद्धं वाशुद्धवर्णं विगतमतिभयं तारयत्येव सिन्धुम् ||
verses.transliteration: nāmaikaṃ yasya vāci smaraṇapathagatāṃ śrotramūlaṃ gataṃ vā | śuddhaṃ vāśuddhavarṇaṃ vigatamātibhayaṃ tārayatyeva sindhum ||
verses.translation: The one name — whether spoken by the voice, whether reached by memory, whether it has entered the root of the ear — pure or impure in pronunciation — crossing all fear, it carries one across the ocean.
verses.hindi: वह एक नाम — चाहे वाणी से बोला जाये, चाहे स्मरण-पथ से प्राप्त हो, चाहे कान की जड़ तक पहुँचे — शुद्ध हो या अशुद्ध उच्चारण — सभी भय को पार करके, वह सागर को पार कराता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana makes the most inclusive possible claim for nama-japa: it works whether spoken, silently remembered, or even merely heard. And — crucially — whether the pronunciation is "pure" (śuddhaṃ) or "impure" (aśuddhavarṇaṃ). This directly addresses the anxiety that non-Sanskritists or those uncertain of correct pronunciation feel about mantra practice. The divine name is not a code that only works when decoded correctly; it is a living reality that responds to the love behind the utterance, not the linguistic precision of it.

verses.hindi: भक्ति से मुझे यथार्थ जाना जाता है — जितना मैं हूँ और जैसा मैं हूँ। इस प्रकार मुझे तत्त्वतः जानकर, वह तत्पश्चात् मुझमें प्रवेश करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana quotes the Bhagavad Gita (18.55) as its ultimate authority — Vishnu's own declaration that bhakti is the means of truly knowing the divine, and that this knowledge leads directly to entry (viśate) into the divine. "Tattvataḥ" — truly, in reality, as it actually is — distinguishes this knowing from intellectual knowledge about the divine. Intellectual knowledge describes; bhakti-jnana reveals. The sequence is precise: bhakti → tattvataḥ-jnanam → entry into the divine. The Narada Purana places this Gita verse at the culmination of its Uttara Khanda to complete the arc: from the nine forms of bhakti, through sankirtana, through music, through the five forms of the divine, through daily practice — everything converges on this single verse.

chapters.title: Book 1 - Adhyaya 7

verses.sanskrit: जन्म मृत्युश्च जरा व्याधिः दुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् | असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु ||
verses.transliteration: janma mṛtyuśca jarā vyādhiḥ duḥkhadoṣānudarśanam | asaktirAnabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu ||
verses.translation: Birth, death, old age, disease — seeing the faults and sorrows in these. Non-attachment, non-clinging toward sons, wife, home and the rest.
verses.hindi: जन्म, मृत्यु, जरा, व्याधि — इनमें दुख और दोषों का दर्शन। पुत्र, पत्नी, घर आदि में अनासक्ति और अनभिष्वंग।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana quotes directly from the Bhagavad Gita (13.8-9) — a passage that the Gita calls "jnanam" (knowledge itself). Birth, death, old age, and disease are not merely medical facts but the structural features of conditioned existence that, when clearly seen, motivate the search for what is unconditional. "Asakti" (non-attachment) and "anabhisvanga" (non-clinging) are not coldness or indifference but the result of truly seeing the impermanence of what one is clinging to. The Narada Purana places this teaching at the heart of its cosmological section: understanding the structure of the cosmos leads naturally to non-attachment from it.

verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः | ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ||
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ | tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram ||

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम गायति वादति नृत्यति ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma gāyati vādati nṛtyati ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He sings, speaks, and dances the sankirtana of Vishnu's name.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। वे विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन गाते, बोलते और नृत्य करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. Bhakti is not merely private devotion but public celebration — singing, speaking, dancing. Narada represents the archetype of the divine communicator who spreads the name of Vishnu everywhere. The Narada Purana places sankirtana (chanting) at the center of the bhakti path.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. Bhakti is not merely private devotion but public celebration — singing, speaking, dancing. Narada represents the archetype of the divine communicator who spreads the name of Vishnu everywhere. The Narada Purana places sankirtana (chanting) at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: नारदो भक्तिमार्गस्य प्रवर्तको दिव्यदूतः | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: nārado bhaktimārgasya pravartako divyadūtaḥ | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Narada is the initiator of the path of bhakti, the divine messenger. He who worships Vishnu with devotion attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: नारद भक्ति मार्ग के प्रवर्तक हैं, दिव्य दूत हैं। जो विष्णु को भक्ति से भजता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. "Divyadūta" — divine messenger. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana's core teaching: Narada is not merely a sage but the divine messenger who initiates the bhakti path, and devotion to Vishnu is the means of liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana identifies Narada as the initiator of the bhakti path and the divine messenger. "Bhaktimārgasya pravartaka" — the one who initiates the path of devotion. "Divyadūta" — divine messenger. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana's core teaching: Narada is not merely a sage but the divine messenger who initiates the bhakti path, and devotion to Vishnu is the means of liberation.

verses.sanskrit: संकीर्तनं विष्णोर्नाम संकीर्तनं नाम तथा | संकीर्तनं नाम स्मरणं संकीर्तनं नाम भक्तिः ||
verses.transliteration: saṅkīrtanaṃ viṣṇornāma saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma tathā | saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma smaraṇaṃ saṅkīrtanaṃ nāma bhaktiḥ ||
verses.translation: Sankirtana of Vishnu's name, sankirtana of the name, sankirtana of remembrance, sankirtana of devotion — all are sankirtana.
verses.hindi: विष्णु के नाम का संकीर्तन, नाम का संकीर्तन, स्मरण का संकीर्तन, भक्ति का संकीर्तन — सब संकीर्तन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. The Narada Purana places sankirtana at the center of the bhakti path.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana defines sankirtana as the chanting of Vishnu's name, the chanting of the name itself, the chanting of remembrance, and the chanting of devotion. The repetition emphasises that all these are forms of sankirtana. Sankirtana is not merely singing but the continuous remembrance of the divine through all forms of practice. The Narada Purana places sankirtana at the center of the bhakti path.

verses.sanskrit: गायति वादति नृत्यति पूजयति शृणोति च | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: gāyati vādati nṛtyati pūjayati śṛṇoti ca | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: Singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, listening — he who worships Vishnu with devotion through these attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: गाते, बोलते, नृत्य करते, पूजा करते, सुनते — जो इन सब से भक्ति से विष्णु का भजन करता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. The verse states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion through these five forms attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana teaching that bhakti can be expressed through multiple modalities. All are valid paths to liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana lists five forms of bhakti practice: singing, speaking, dancing, worshipping, and listening. The verse states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion through these five forms attain the supreme state. This is the Narada Purana teaching that bhakti can be expressed through multiple modalities. All are valid paths to liberation.

verses.sanskrit: सप्त स्वराः समुद्भूताः ब्रह्माण्डस्य नादतः | षड्जं च ऋषभं चैव गान्धारं मध्यमं तथा | पञ्चमं च धैवतं च निषादं सप्तमं विदुः ||
verses.transliteration: sapta svarāḥ samudbhūtāḥ brahmāṇḍasya nādataḥ | ṣaḍjaṃ ca ṛṣabhaṃ caiva gāndhāraṃ madhyamaṃ tathā | pañcamaṃ ca dhhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ saptamaṃ viduḥ ||
verses.translation: The seven notes arose from the sound of the cosmos — Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni — these seven are known.
verses.hindi: सात स्वर ब्रह्माण्ड के नाद से उत्पन्न हुए — षड्ज, ऋषभ, गान्धार, मध्यम, पञ्चम, धैवत, निषाद — ये सात जाने जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's cosmological account of the seven musical notes: they did not arise from human invention but from the primordial sound (nāda) of the cosmos itself — the vibration of the Brahmaanda (cosmic egg). Each note is thus not an acoustic convention but a frequency of existence. Sa (Shadja — born from six) is the tonic, the ground; each subsequent note is a specific relationship to that ground. The entire raga system is a map of how consciousness moves away from and returns to its own source. Narada's teaching: when you sing in tune, you are resonating with the structure of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र मनो याति तत्र तत्र समाहितम् | तत्र तत्र परं ब्रह्म तत्र तत्र जनार्दनः ||
verses.transliteration: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatra samāhitam | tatra tatra paraṃ brahma tatra tatra janārdanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Wherever the mind goes — there is the collected (concentrated one). There is supreme Brahman there. There is Janardana (Vishnu) there.
verses.hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ मन जाता है — वहाँ-वहाँ वह समाहित (एकाग्र) है। वहाँ-वहाँ परम ब्रह्म है। वहाँ-वहाँ जनार्दन है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's radical teaching on the ubiquity of the divine: wherever the mind moves, Brahman is already there. This is not a consolation but a metaphysical assertion. If Brahman is truly all-pervading (vibhu, sarvavyapin), then there is no location — mental or physical — where Brahman is absent. The implication for bhakti is transformative: you cannot leave the divine. You can only fail to notice it. The practice of smaranam (remembrance) is thus not about bringing the divine into consciousness but about recognising what is already and always present there.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वदा सर्वभावेन भजनीयो जनार्दनः | भक्त्या परमया चैव प्रेम्णा च परमेण च ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo janārdanaḥ | bhaktyā paramayā caiva premṇā ca parameṇa ca ||
verses.translation: Janardana (Vishnu) should be worshipped always, with all one's being — with supreme devotion and with the highest love.
verses.hindi: जनार्दन का सदा, सर्वभाव से, परम भक्ति से और परम प्रेम से भजन करना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: Three qualifiers pile upon one another: "sarvadā" (always — not just in puja or in difficulty), "sarvabhāvena" (with all one's being — not a compartmentalised religious activity but the whole person), "paramayā bhaktyā" (with supreme devotion) and "parameṇa premṇā" (with the highest love). The Narada Purana insists that bhakti is not a technique or a ritual but a total orientation of one's existence. Loving the divine "always and with all one's being" is not a demand — it is a description of what genuine bhakti is. When it is genuine, it is naturally total.

verses.sanskrit: स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवपूजनम् | वैश्वदेवं तथातिथ्यं नित्यकर्मेति कीर्तितम् ||
verses.transliteration: snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devapūjanam | vaiśvadevaṃ tathātithyaṃ nityakarmeti kīrtitam ||
verses.translation: Bathing, giving, japa, fire-offering, self-study, worship of the deity, the Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings), and hospitality — these are declared the daily duties (nitya-karma).
verses.hindi: स्नान, दान, जप, होम, स्वाध्याय, देवपूजन, वैश्वदेव और अतिथि-सेवा — ये नित्यकर्म कहे गये हैं।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana's eight-fold daily practice — nitya-karma — is a complete architecture of a life oriented toward the divine. Snana (purification of body), dana (purification through giving), japa (purification of speech/mind through repetition), homa (fire-offering — the discipline of sacrifice), svadhyaya (self-study — reading and contemplating the sacred), deva-pujana (formal worship), Vaishvadeva (offering to all beings — the recognition of the divine in all forms of life), and atithya (hospitality — honouring the divine in the stranger). Together these eight cover the full range of human activity: body, resources, mind, speech, knowledge, ritual, ecology, and social relationship.
verses.wordMeaning: The Narada Purana's eight-fold daily practice — nitya-karma — is a complete architecture of a life oriented toward the divine. verses.sanskrit: नामैकं यस्य वाचि स्मरणपथगतं श्रोत्रमूलं गतं वा | शुद्धं वाशुद्धवर्णं विगतमतिभयं तारयत्येव सिन्धुम् ||
verses.transliteration: nāmaikaṃ yasya vāci smaraṇapathagatāṃ śrotramūlaṃ gataṃ vā | śuddhaṃ vāśuddhavarṇaṃ vigatamātibhayaṃ tārayatyeva sindhum ||
verses.translation: The one name — whether spoken by the voice, whether reached by memory, whether it has entered the root of the ear — pure or impure in pronunciation — crossing all fear, it carries one across the ocean.
verses.hindi: वह एक नाम — चाहे वाणी से बोला जाये, चाहे स्मरण-पथ से प्राप्त हो, चाहे कान की जड़ तक पहुँचे — शुद्ध हो या अशुद्ध उच्चारण — सभी भय को पार करके, वह सागर को पार कराता है।
verses.commentary: The Narada Purana makes the most inclusive possible claim for nama-japa: it works whether spoken, silently remembered, or even merely heard. And — crucially — whether the pronunciation is "pure" (śuddhaṃ) or "impure" (aśuddhavarṇaṃ). This directly addresses the anxiety that non-Sanskritists or those uncertain of correct pronunciation feel about mantra practice. The divine name is not a code that only works when decoded correctly; it is a living reality that responds to the love behind the utterance, not the linguistic precision of it.
